thread:
Michelle: Quick heads-up — noticed a lot of noisy autofallback churn on the eu-west hostgroup since the rollout. Logs show rapid flip between primary model/v2 and fallback v1-a. Can we chew on whether debounce or hysteresis belongs in the policy or in the router?
Raj: Ugh, saw that too. Happens when transient 500 bursts hit the model cache miss path.
Lina: My worry: add debounce at router layer = simpler for ops, but we lose per-customer granularity.
Sam: Agree. If we do per-route debounce, we need a small state-store. That complicates private deployments.
Michelle: Right — also we need auditability. Operators want to see a clean trace of why we flipped during the window (signal history).
Raj: Could we store a compact event buffer with 1s granularity per route for N=30s and expose it in the rollouts UI? Example: event stream of {t,status,err_class,latency_ms}.
Lina: That sounds fine. UX question — on the console do we show the buffered signals inline on the rollout card or as a detail flyout?
Sam: Flyout + timeline seems less noisy. Card shows current state + last flip reason summarized. Flyout has the raw buffer with mini-graphs.
Michelle: For the policy model, propose debounce + hysteresis: require X signals in Y sec to trigger fallback, and require Z healthy signals in W sec to switch back. Keeps oscillation low.
Raj: Here's a quick config sketch we tested locally:
```json
{
  "policy_name": "auto_fallback",
  "trigger": {
    "err_classes": ["5xx","model_cache_miss"],
    "threshold": 5,
    "window_secs": 10
  },
  "hysteresis": {
    "recover_threshold": 8,
    "recover_window_secs": 30
  },
  "debounce_ms": 2500
}
```
Lina: Nice. Does debounce_ms belong in the policy or router config? If in policy then it becomes part of the audit trail.
Michelle: I vote policy. That way the rollback/playbook references the exact config that triggered the action.
Sam: Implementation nuance: policy-driven debounce needs to be enforced by the routing decision path before it emits the fallback event. We should avoid racing where two routers both decide to fallback at the same time.
Raj: ops-bot: created incident I-2026-112 for noisy autofallback, attached initial traces and sample buffers. :eyes:
ops-bot: I-2026-112 created by Raj — priority P2. Links: https://internal/trace/I-2026-112
Lina: UX ask: include a small "Why did we switch?" pill on outbound traces that references the policy snapshot id and the buffered events that crossed threshold.
Michelle: Good. Also add an affordance to "simulate signals" in the rollout dry-run so PMs/QA can reproduce flapping without hitting prod.
Sam: Backend: we can reuse the existing short-term ring buffer used by the quota service. Should add a TTL and compressed storage to avoid explosion.
Raj: One more: telemetry — emit both the raw event count and the decision reason metric. E.g. `fallback.decision{reason=err_rate,policy=v2}` + `fallback.buffer_count`. That helps dashboards and alerts.
Michelle: Agree. Lina can you mock the console layout? I'll draft the policy protobuf and an RFC for where debounce lives.
Lina: On it. Will post a quick Figma in #design later today.
Michelle: Thanks — target to prototype by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Note: new canary of routing-service with ring-buffer export will deploy to staging at 1719997600.
Sam: Great — I'll run the dry-run tests after the canary lands.
Michelle: Closing loop: if anyone sees more noisy flips, ping this thread and tag I-2026-112.
